description.value: The study examined behavioral and fMRI BOLD responses during cognitive reappraisal of looming harsh faces, social criticism, and autobiographical negative self-beliefs in patients with generalized social anxiety disorder and healthy controls.

design.value: A between-group fMRI study comparing 27 unmedicated adults with generalized SAD and 27 healthy controls during three socio-emotional tasks. Each task included React and Reappraise conditions, and the study analyzed behavioral ratings, BOLD signal magnitude, and early versus late BOLD responses.

description.value: This questionnaire assesses both fear and behavioral avoidance of social situations.

name.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

description.value: Two PhD-level clinical psychologists assessed each potential participant using the Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version.
After each trial, participants rated “How negative do you feel?” using a 1 to 5 button-response scale, where 1 = not at all and 5 = very much.

source_definition.value: The contrast of Reappraise versus React conditions.
A 2 Group (SAD, HC) between-group t-test of Reappraise versus React in SAD versus HC.
Early responses were the first three time points, 0–4.5 s; late responses were the last two or three time points, 4.5–7.5 s or 4.5–9 s, depending on the task.

name.value: Percent reduction in negative emotion ratings

source_definition.value: Percent reduction in negative emotion when reappraising.
Late dorsomedial PFC BOLD responses during Reappraise versus React.

association_direction.value: positive association with percent reduction in negative emotion ratings in SAD patients

description.value: 27 (12 women) unmedicated adults who met DSM-IV-TR criteria for primary generalized SAD; the selected subgroup had the highest social anxiety symptom severity.

inclusion_criteria.value: Met clinical diagnostic criteria for a principal diagnosis of current generalized SAD, defined as greater than moderate anxiety/fear for five or more distinct social situations.
Selected from patients eligible for the study based on the highest social anxiety symptom severity; subgroup LSAS-SR scores ranged from 85–102.

exclusion_criteria.value: Current psychiatric disorders other than SAD, generalized anxiety disorder, agoraphobia without a history of panic attacks, dysthymia, or specific phobia.

recruitment_method.value: Clinician referrals and advertisements on community and online bulletin boards.

medical_condition.value: Primary current generalized social anxiety disorder.
Current Axis-I co-morbidity included two with panic attacks, two with generalized anxiety disorder, two with dysthymia, and two with specific phobia.
Past Axis-I co-morbidity included six with major depression, one with post-traumatic stress disorder, four with substance abuse, and one with eating disorder.

diagnostic_instrument.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

clinical_characteristics.value: The subgroup of 27 SAD patients had LSAS-SR scores ranging from 85–102; the range for the whole eligible patient group was 66–102.

medication_status.value: Unmedicated; minimum of three months since stopping pharmacotherapy. Seven patients reported past pharmacotherapy.

education_summary.value: Patients and HC did not differ significantly in years of education.

description.value: 27 (13 women) healthy controls with no lifetime history of psychiatric disorders.

inclusion_criteria.value: No current or past history of DSM-IV disorders.

exclusion_criteria.value: HC were not permitted to meet criteria for any current or past psychiatric disorders.

medical_condition.value: No lifetime history of psychiatric disorders.

diagnostic_instrument.value: Anxiety Disorders Interview Schedule for DSM-IV-TR Lifetime version (ADIS-IV-L)

clinical_characteristics.value: Healthy controls had no current or past history of DSM-IV disorders.

education_summary.value: Patients and HC did not differ significantly in years of education.

task_description.value: A socio-emotional fMRI task consisting of 24 trials in which participants viewed looming harsh faces and either reacted normally or reappraised their emotional response.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed either to react to the faces by engaging in the picture, “Just let yourself feel,” and thinking, “This person is upset with me; angry with me,” or to reappraise their emotion, for example by thinking, “Maybe this person just had a bad day.”

stimuli.value: Color photos of faces displaying Ekman facial action coded anger and contempt facial expressions; each harsh facial stimulus appeared to move closer to the participant to simulate looming.

task_performance_measures.value: Negative emotion rating after each trial using a 1–5 button response scale.

task_description.value: A socio-emotional fMRI task using videotaped actors delivering social criticism or praise; only the 7.5-second evaluation period of social criticism trials was included in the current analysis.

instructions.value: Participants were told to react to the social criticism by reflecting on how the statement represents something true about themselves, or to reappraise their emotion, for example by thinking, “this is not always true,” or “this is only a thought, not a fact.”

stimuli.value: Videotaped actors delivering social criticism and social praise with harsh or happy evaluation-congruent facial expressions. The stimuli were delivered by five male and five female actors, seven Anglo-Americans and three Asian-Americans, aged 23 to 50 years.

task_performance_measures.value: Negative emotion rating after each video clip using a 1–5 button response scale.

task_description.value: A socio-emotional fMRI task in which participants reacted to or reframed autobiographical social anxiety-related negative self-beliefs embedded in unfolding written situations.

instructions.value: Participants were trained to react to the negative self-beliefs by reflecting on how the belief represents something true about themselves, or to reappraise their reaction by thinking of a positive coping statement that directly challenges the thoughts: “try to re-interpret the statement so it is less negative and toxic for you.”

stimuli.value: Five situations: one experimenter-composed neutral situation and four participant-generated autobiographical social anxiety situations characterized by social anxiety, humiliation, and/or embarrassment. Each situation included 16 sentences describing the situation and 10 negative self-beliefs in uppercase letters.

task_performance_measures.value: Negative emotion rating after each negative self-belief using a 1–5 button response scale.

description.value: Three-dimensional high-resolution anatomical scans were acquired using a fast spin-echo spoiled gradient recall sequence.

AFNI preprocessing included analysis of potential outliers, volume registration to a base image, motion correction, 4 mm isotropic Gaussian spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering at 0.011 Hz, linear detrending, and conversion into BOLD signal percentage change in each voxel. The first four images of each functional run were excluded for T2* equilibration effects; the Criticism and Belief runs were concatenated before statistical analysis.

hrf_model.value: Cohen’s gamma variate model of the hemodynamic response function

model_settings.value: Regressors for the React and Reappraise conditions were convolved with the Cohen’s gamma variate hemodynamic response function. Baseline parameters removed mean, linear, and quadratic trends and motion-related variance in the BOLD signal. BOLD signal intensity was computed as percentage of signal change.

model_type.value: random-effects model with between-group and one-sample t-tests

model_settings.value: Individual brain maps were converted to Talairach atlas space and second-level group statistical parametric maps were produced according to a random-effects model. Whole-brain between-group analyses used a voxel-wise P <0.005 and cluster volume >244 mm³ to protect against false-positive cluster detection at P <0.01. Common responses were identified using one-sample t-tests of Reappraise versus React separately in SAD and HC.

software.value: AlphaSim Monte Carlo simulation bootstrapping program

model_type.value: between-group t-tests of temporal BOLD responses

model_settings.value: Masks were created from significant clusters separately for each task; percent signal change was extracted for Reappraise and React at the individual-subject level; Reappraise minus React was calculated; early and late time points were averaged for each subject; and between-group t-tests were run separately for early and late averaged responses for each task.

Associations between late DMPFC BOLD responses during Reappraise versus React and percent reduction in negative emotion ratings were examined separately in SAD patients and HC, with a test comparing the correlations.

estimator.value: correlation coefficient r and Zdiff comparison
